import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import io

# Load the dataset from the string
data = """amount,is_fraud,transaction_type,hour_of_day
115.02,0,refund,22
44.37,0,payment,5
144.25,0,transfer,21
536.22,0,payment,17
38.43,0,payment,5
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a professional and clean style for the plot
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a bubble chart to visualize all dimensions of the data
# x-axis: hour_of_day
# y-axis: amount
# color: transaction_type
# size: amount (to emphasize larger transactions)
# style: is_fraud (to distinguish fraudulent transactions, although all are 0 in this sample)
plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='hour_of_day',
    y='amount',
    hue='transaction_type',
    size='amount',
    style='is_fraud',
    sizes=(100, 1500),  # Range of bubble sizes
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.8,
    ax=ax,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1
)

# Enhance the plot with titles and labels for clarity
ax.set_title('Transaction Analysis by Hour, Type, and Amount', fontsize=18, weight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Transaction Amount ($)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)

# Improve the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Manually reorder and title legend sections for better readability
legend = ax.legend(
    handles=handles,
    labels=labels,
    title='Legend',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    fontsize=12,
    title_fontsize=14,
    shadow=True,
    frameon=True
)
legend.get_title().set_fontweight('bold')

# Set x-axis limits and ticks for clarity
ax.set_xlim(0, 24)
ax.set_xticks(range(0, 25, 2))

# Add a light grid for better readability
ax.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

# Ensure the layout is tight and all elements fit
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend

# Save the resulting visualization to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

# Close the plot to free up memory
plt.close()
